title: The Allowance Made Against the Charge on a Given-Up Protection Plan
content:
An allowance is made against the charge a Pass and Trip Protection plan is raised for being given up, settled
from the standing of the covered holding under the Season Pass Programme and from what the plan's protection
account shows paid.

| The records show | The allowance |
| --- | --- |
| The covered holding's record showing it given up in the season | The whole of the plan's cancellation fee |
| The protection account carrying a payment matched to a premium entry, and the covered holding standing active | 25.00 per cent of the plan's cancellation fee |
| Any other case | Nothing |

**Reading the schedule.** The rows are read in the order given, so a covered holding given up in the season
carries the whole of the fee as an allowance whatever the protection account shows. The second row is
compound: at least one payment matched to a premium entry must stand on the plan's protection account and the
covered holding must at the same time stand active. A covered holding standing neither given up nor active, or
one standing active with no matched payment on the plan, falls to the third row and carries no allowance.

**Worked figures (hypothetical inputs).** On a plan whose cancellation fee is 25.00 USD, a covered holding
given up in the season carries an allowance of 25.00 USD; a covered holding standing active with one payment
matched to a premium entry on the plan carries an allowance of 6.25 USD; and a covered holding standing active
with no such payment carries an allowance of 0.00 USD.
